verses.text: I know you can do anything. Nothing can stop what you’ve decided to do.
You asked, ‘Who is this, hiding my counsel without knowledge?’ I spoke about things I didn’t understand, things too wonderful for me to know.
You said, ‘Listen now, and I’ll speak. I’ll ask the questions, and you’ll answer me.’
I had heard about you before, but now I see you with my own eyes.
So I reject what I said and repent in dust and ashes.
After the LORD finished speaking to Job, he said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “I’m angry with you and your two friends. You haven’t spoken rightly about me the way my servant Job has.

So take seven bulls and seven rams to my servant Job and offer them as a burnt offering for yourselves. My servant Job will pray for you, and I’ll accept his prayer, so I won’t deal with you as your foolishness deserves. You haven’t spoken rightly about me the way my servant Job has.”
So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite did what the LORD told them, and the LORD accepted Job’s prayer.
When Job prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his prosperity and gave him twice as much as he’d had before.

All his brothers and sisters and everyone who’d known him before came and shared a meal at his house. They comforted him over all the suffering the LORD had brought on him. Each gave him a piece of money and a gold ring.
The LORD blessed the later years of Job’s life more than the early ones. Job had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand pairs of oxen, and a thousand female donkeys.
He also had seven sons and three daughters.
He named his first daughter Jemimah, the second Keziah, and the third Keren Happuch.
Nowhere in the land were there women as beautiful as Job’s daughters. Their father gave them an inheritance alongside their brothers.
Job lived another hundred and forty years and saw his children and their descendants to the fourth generation.
Job died at a good old age, having lived a full life.
